Executive summary

WallpaperControl 1.8.3 builds cleanly and all 121 custom regression checks pass, but the application is not yet reliably protected against failures at the boundaries between its native wallpaper state, custom renderer, timers and forms. This independent source audit identifies 28 substantive findings: 0 Critical, 4 High, 20 Medium and 4 Low. Counts represent distinct issues, not analyzer occurrences.

The highest priorities are acquiring a usable renderer before disabling native scheduling (H1), coherent multi-monitor behavior (H2), advancing past an unreadable image (H3), and bounded processing of calendar input (H4). Reproduced lifecycle/UI defects include a calendar refresh timer that never starts, an ineffective private-URL mask, a broken update action, lost early thumbnail loads, and a weather timer restarted after disposal.

No Critical issue was established at the required confidence and impact level. Several failure paths could escalate to hangs or lost state under particular external conditions; those conditions and confidence limits are stated individually. No confirmed privilege escalation or arbitrary code execution was found. This is not a guarantee of absence.

The review used current implementation, source-level execution tracing, the complete custom regression harness, expanded analyzers, localization parity checks and isolated audit probes. Prior audit reports were not used. No tracked source, project configuration or suppression was changed, and no commit was created.

High findings

H1 · The app stops Windows scheduling before it knows its renderer is usable

HighLikelyFix effort: Medium

File: WallpaperControl/Wallpaper/PersistentDesktopTransitionManager.cs
Method / type: InitializeHostAsync / ApplyAsync
Lines: 20–57, 80–105; MainForm.Scheduler.cs:18–60; PersistentDesktopWallpaperHost.cs:981–1054

Failure mechanism

StartCustomSlideshowEngine calls SetWallpaper(null, current) and marks the custom engine active. Later, InitializeHostAsync can return false when Progman or its direct SHELLDLL_DefView child is absent or native attachment fails. ApplyAsync simply returns; it never invokes DirectWallpaperTransition or restores Windows scheduling. The UI continues to report an active slideshow. Initialization also publishes persistentHost before Initialize succeeds; an exception while loading the initial image leaves a non-disposed but incompletely initialized host that subsequent calls accept as ready.

Circumstances / confidence

Explorer startup/restart, a shell layout without the expected direct child, or a native/initial image failure. The failure branches are confirmed by source; affected Windows shell configurations were not reproduced on this desktop.

Recommended fix

Make renderer initialization transactional and represent readiness explicitly. Acquire a usable renderer before taking scheduling ownership; on failure use the native direct path or restore native scheduling and show one actionable status. Dispose a partially initialized host in catch/finally, and await one shared initialization task.

Regression protection

Inject attach=false and a LoadFrame exception. Verify native scheduling stays active or a direct fallback changes the image, and the next initialization can succeed.

H2 · Custom slideshow freezes secondary monitors and does not implement Span

HighConfirmedFix effort: Large

File: WallpaperControl/Wallpaper/PersistentDesktopWallpaperHost.cs
Method / type: Initialize / EnsureDesktopPlacement / LoadFrame
Lines: 46–49, 101–125, 902–917, 1124–1137; MainForm.Scheduler.cs:40–45; MainForm.Wallpaper.cs:37–46

Failure mechanism

The application first sets one current image for every monitor and stops native scheduling. Its only persistent host has primary-screen dimensions, is positioned at (0,0), and transitions only its own bitmap. No transition commits a new native wallpaper for the remaining monitors. Span is rendered as Fill against the same primary-sized canvas. There is no display-change handler to rebuild frame dimensions when topology or resolution changes.

Circumstances / confidence

Any active custom slideshow on multiple displays; Span selection; display resize or hot-plug. Source confirms the missing per-monitor update path. No physical multi-monitor visual test was performed.

Recommended fix

Define monitor ownership explicitly. Implement a virtual-desktop canvas or one host per monitor, including negative origins and per-monitor DPI. Keep other monitors on a coherent native fallback until that exists, and recreate/re-render frames after topology changes.

Regression protection

Test two displays with distinct wallpapers, primary-display changes, negative coordinates, mixed DPI, Span and hot-unplug.

H3 · One unreadable image can trap the sequential slideshow on the same failure

HighConfirmedFix effort: Medium

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/MainForm/MainForm.Wallpaper.cs
Method / type: AdvanceCustomWallpaperAsync
Lines: 161–213, 228–249; PersistentDesktopWallpaperHost.cs:209–211, 880–886

Failure mechanism

Candidates are accepted by filename extension and selected relative to the last successfully displayed path. If decoding the next file throws, the displayed path never advances. The next scheduled or manual forward request therefore selects the same file again and shows another modal error. A corrupt or partially written supported image can block every later good image in a non-shuffled folder. The decoder failure mechanism is independent of whether a particular OS supports WebP.

Circumstances / confidence

Shuffle disabled and the next ordered image is corrupt, still being copied, or unsupported by the actual Image.FromFile decoder. Automatic ticks can repeatedly raise modal dialogs while the app is in the tray.

Recommended fix

Try other candidates with a bounded attempt count, cache transient failures with a retry policy, and report automatic failures non-modally. Centralize accepted formats around actual decoder capability; do not count an extension-only check as decoding validation.

Regression protection

Folder fixture: valid A, corrupt B.jpg, valid C. Advancing from A must reach C without an infinite retry or repeated modal prompts; repairing B must eventually make it eligible again.

H4 · Calendar feeds have no practical resource limits before parsing and drawing

HighLikelyFix effort: Medium

File: WallpaperControl/Services/IcsCalendarProvider.cs
Method / type: LoadSourceAsync / GetUpcoming / ExpandForDailyDisplay
Lines: 182–202, 216–237, 268–283; CalendarWidgetForm.cs:178–190, 304–335

Failure mechanism

HTTP bodies are buffered as strings with no application size cap. A 90-day time window does not bound the number of recurrence instances: a dense RRULE can generate millions. Cancellation is not checked inside parsing, expansion or sorting. GetUpcoming materializes all events and expands full all-day durations before selecting days; maxEntries limits days, not rows. The widget then allocates a bitmap whose height grows with every row, outside the refresh exception handler. Dense or hostile feeds can exhaust CPU/memory or fail in async-void rendering.

Circumstances / confidence

A configured subscription delivers a large body, dense recurrence, very long all-day range, or many events on one day. This is an external-feed availability risk, not an unauthenticated remote code-execution finding. No destructive exhaustion test was run.

Recommended fix

Bound response bytes, source count, event count, recurrence expansion and all-day expansion; clamp expansion to the visible horizon before materialization. Enforce cancellation/time budgets, cap rendered rows/height and show an overflow indicator. Catch rendering failures at the UI event boundary.

Regression protection

Use bounded synthetic feeds covering dense SECONDLY recurrence, a long all-day range, oversized response, cancellation and hundreds of same-day events. Assert bounded work and a usable widget.

Medium findings

M1 · Statistics selection changes the hidden native wallpaper, not the visible host

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Medium

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/MainForm/MainForm.History.cs
Method / type: SetWallpaperFromStatistics
Lines: 18–53; MainForm.Wallpaper.cs:18–26; PersistentDesktopTransitionManager.cs:140–143

Failure mechanism

The statistics callback calls only IDesktopWallpaper.SetWallpaper. The visible persistent host keeps its old frame and CurrentWallpaperPath, which GetCurrentWallpaperPath prefers. The custom engine is not stopped and its timer is not re-armed or paused; IsSlideshowCurrentlyActive normally sees no native slideshow after the custom engine took ownership. Thus selecting a wallpaper in Statistics can appear to do nothing and the next automatic transition proceeds from the old image.

Circumstances / confidence

Select a statistics row while the persistent host/custom slideshow is active.

Recommended fix

Route this command through the same application-level wallpaper change operation as the scheduler. Explicitly choose whether manual selection pauses or continues, update the visible host/native state atomically, and record the actual committed image.

Regression protection

Select a different image through Statistics during idle and during a transition; verify visible image, next deadline, pause state, history and view counts agree.

M2 · Manual pause and pin leave an in-flight transition running

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Medium

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/MainForm/MainForm.Slideshow.cs
Method / type: PauseSlideshow / PinButton_Click
Lines: 29–39, 163–201; MainForm.Wallpaper.cs:213–249; PersistentDesktopWallpaperHost.cs:284–321

Failure mechanism

Manual pause disables only the scheduling timer. Pin disables the custom engine and sets Windows to the old committed path, but neither action suspends/cancels the host's animation timer. The animation can subsequently replace the displayed frame and commit the next path while the UI says paused or pinned. Pin is also available through the tray during fullscreen suspension; a suspended transition can finish on fullscreen exit after pinning. Related shutdown paths do not pass an owner cancellation token and post-await cleanup can still touch UI state.

Circumstances / confidence

Press Pause or Pin during a 0.5–5 second transition, including a transition suspended by fullscreen. This ordering follows directly from the separate timers and missing cancellation.

Recommended fix

Serialize user actions with transition completion, or cancel/settle the current animation before changing pause/pin ownership. Use a form-lifetime cancellation token, stop incoming commands before shutdown, and guard post-await UI work.

Regression protection

Drive pause, pin, folder change and exit at each animation phase. Assert that the selected pause/pin image cannot be replaced by an older pending operation.

M3 · Overdue deadlines are replayed and can create a zero-delay callback loop

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Small

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/MainForm/MainForm.Scheduler.cs
Method / type: ProcessPreciseCustomSlideshowTick / ArmCustomSlideshowPreciseTimer
Lines: 98–114, 150–158, 185–209

Failure mechanism

The next deadline is calculated from the old target rather than a boundary after the current time. After sleep or a forward clock jump, multiple targets remain in the past. Remaining time is clamped to zero, and the change-running branch re-arms that same overdue target at zero while an animation is active. This repeatedly queues UI callbacks and then rapidly catches up missed wallpaper changes instead of returning to a future boundary.

Circumstances / confidence

Resume after missing multiple intervals, or move the system clock forward while the app runs. Fullscreen exit recalculates deadlines, but ordinary system suspend has no equivalent recovery handler.

Recommended fix

Skip missed intervals: compute the next deadline strictly after the observed current time. When a change is running, wait for completion or use a bounded retry delay rather than re-arming an expired target at zero.

customSlideshowNextChange = GetNextAlignedChange(DateTime.Now, milliseconds);
// A running transition should re-arm on completion, not at zero delay.

Regression protection

Inject a clock advancing several hours and an in-flight transition. Assert at most one catch-up change and a future deadline, with no tight timer loop.

M4 · Calendar refresh is never scheduled on the initial widget instance

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Small

File: WallpaperControl/Widgets/CalendarWidgetForm.cs
Method / type: constructor / Apply / OnShown
Lines: 53–64, 95–112, 153–160

Failure mechanism

The constructor calls Apply before the form has a handle. Apply starts refreshTimer only when a handle already exists. OnShown renders and refreshes once but never starts the timer. WidgetManager's initial SetActivitySuspended(false) is a no-op because false is already the state. Consequently the calendar stays at its initial snapshot until a later settings Apply or a suspend/resume cycle starts the timer.

Circumstances / confidence

Calendar enabled on application startup with no subsequent settings or fullscreen state change. Isolated probe against the current assembly confirmed timer=False both after construction and after OnShown.

Recommended fix

Start the refresh timer in OnShown when not suspended/disposed; make timer state a single consequence of active lifecycle state rather than incidental Apply calls.

Regression protection

Create and show a fresh calendar widget, wait via an injected short interval, and verify multiple refreshes; repeat for initially suspended, resumed and disposed states.

M5 · The release-page button returns a result that neither caller accepts

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Trivial

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/UpdateDialog.cs
Method / type: UpdateDialog constructor
Lines: 145–150; MainForm.Updates.cs:103–115; SettingsForm.General.cs:60–69

Failure mechanism

The View Release button returns DialogResult.OK. Both automatic and manual update callers open the release URL only for DialogResult.Yes. Clicking the intended button therefore closes the dialog without opening the release page. A probe confirmed the actual AcceptButton result is OK.

Circumstances / confidence

Any successful check that reports a newer release, followed by View Release or Enter.

Recommended fix

Use one agreed result in the dialog and both callers, preferably OK for acceptance. Add a contract test covering the dialog button and caller decision.

if (answer == DialogResult.OK && result.ReleaseUri != null)
{
    // Open the validated release URL.
}

Regression protection

Inject UpdateAvailable and activate the release button; assert the expected URL is launched exactly once.

M6 · Private calendar subscription URLs are displayed despite the masking setting

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Small

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/SettingsForm/SettingsForm.Initialization.cs
Method / type: calendar source TextBox construction
Lines: 1287–1315, 1333–1340

Failure mechanism

Both URL text boxes combine Multiline=true with UseSystemPasswordChar=true. The native multiline edit control does not apply password masking, so the Show/Hide toggle does not provide the expected concealment. The current-machine probe returned EM_GETPASSWORDCHAR=0 for this combination versus 42 for a single-line password control. URLs can contain bearer-style calendar access tokens.

Circumstances / confidence

Opening Calendar settings while screen-sharing, recording or with someone nearby. This is display exposure; DPAPI-at-rest protection remains valid.

Recommended fix

Use a list of separately masked single-line URL entries with an explicit reveal action, or a dedicated multiline editor opened only after reveal. Do not rely on the unsupported combination.

Regression protection

Verify rendered concealment and native masking for both calendar URL lists; test reveal/hide and screen-reader behavior with synthetic secrets.

M7 · The renderer ignores the loaded wallpaper-position setting

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Small

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/MainForm/MainForm.SlideshowOptions.cs
Method / type: LoadWallpaperPosition / UpdateWallpaperPositionDisplay
Lines: 131–162, 169–218, 255–256; PersistentDesktopTransitionManager.cs:11–12, 38–39

Failure mechanism

The manager defaults to Fill. Startup reads Windows' position and updates the combo while loading suppresses its change handler, but never calls SetWallpaperPosition. Later external changes also update only the combo under loading. Only a user-driven combo change informs the host. The visible image can therefore be cropped as Fill while the UI says Fit, Center, Tile or Stretch.

Circumstances / confidence

Start with a non-Fill Windows wallpaper position, or change position externally while the app runs.

Recommended fix

Pass the successfully read position into the renderer at startup and whenever an external position change is accepted; re-render both transition frames consistently when position changes mid-animation.

Regression protection

Start with each supported position and verify pixels/aspect ratio; change the position externally and during a transition.

M8 · Failed folder activation is treated as a successful state change

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Medium

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/MainForm/MainForm.Folders.cs
Method / type: SetWallpaperFolder / ApplyNewWallpaperFolder
Lines: 406–437, 479–543; MainForm.Slideshow.cs:130–145, 230–263

Failure mechanism

SetWallpaperFolder catches errors and returns void. Its callers cannot distinguish failure: ApplyNewWallpaperFolder clears history/undo and saves the new path before activation, then starts/advances using whatever folderTextBox still contains. ResumeSlideshowAsync waits and returns true even when SetWallpaperFolder failed internally. Runtime state and saved folder can diverge, and close-after-resume can proceed despite a failed restore.

Circumstances / confidence

A folder disappears after selection, shell item creation fails, or Windows rejects a slideshow operation.

Recommended fix

Return a typed success/error result or propagate the exception. Commit folder, history, undo and persisted state only after activation succeeds; make resume and shutdown handoff consume the result.

Regression protection

Inject failures in shell item creation and SetSlideshow. Verify old settings/history remain, resume returns false and no unrelated folder is advanced.

M9 · A manual update check can show dialogs after its settings owner has closed

MediumLikelyFix effort: Small

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/SettingsForm/SettingsForm.General.cs
Method / type: CheckForUpdatesButton_Click
Lines: 18–104; SettingsForm.cs:252–268

Failure mechanism

Only the check button is disabled. The dialog can be cancelled/disposed while CheckAsync is pending; no owner cancellation token or disposed check precedes the result dialogs. On completion the handler reads disposed controls and calls ShowDialog(this). If that throws, the catch repeats another ShowDialog with the same disposed owner outside any further catch. Depending on native owner handling this yields a stale dialog or an unhandled async-void exception.

Circumstances / confidence

Start a slow manual update check and immediately close Settings. The continuation path is present; its exact native outcome was not exercised with live networking.

Recommended fix

Cancel the check on form close/dispose and return after await if the form is disposing/disposed or cancellation was requested. Do not create an error dialog from the catch when its owner is gone.

Regression protection

Inject a delayed result and close the owner before completion; assert no dialog, no recreated handle and no unhandled UI exception.

M10 · A disposed weather widget restarts its timer after cancellation

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Small

File: WallpaperControl/Widgets/WeatherWidgetForm.cs
Method / type: OnShown / Dispose
Lines: 96–100, 147–195, 411–419

Failure mechanism

OnShown awaits the first refresh and then starts timer whenever activitySuspended is false. Dispose cancels the refresh and disposes the timer, but RefreshWeatherAsync absorbs cancellation; the OnShown continuation still starts the timer. WinForms Timer can be restarted after Dispose. A fake-HTTP probe against the current assembly produced IsDisposed=True and timer.Enabled=True, retaining a useless timer/widget after it is disabled.

Circumstances / confidence

Disable/cancel-preview a weather widget while its initial request is pending, then remain in the application.

Recommended fix

After the initial await, check IsDisposed, Disposing and an explicit lifetime flag before starting the timer. Prefer starting it before the refresh under a single lifecycle controller, and make disposal idempotent.

Regression protection

Block the initial HTTP request, dispose the widget, deliver cancellation, pump the UI loop and assert the timer remains disabled and the widget is collectible.

M11 · Early thumbnail completions permanently suppress those thumbnails

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Small

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/StatisticsForm.cs
Method / type: QueueThumbnailLoad
Lines: 1057–1059, 1482–1484, 2321–2389

Failure mechanism

RefreshStatistics queues loads in the constructor before ShowDialog creates a form handle. A fast worker sees !IsHandleCreated, disposes its result and returns without removing the path from thumbnailLoading. Later refreshes skip that path forever. The isolated probe constructed the real form, let its tiny-image load finish, created the handle and observed cache=0/loading=1. There is also no lifecycle recheck inside the dispatched callback, so close/reset can race ownership transfer.

Circumstances / confidence

Fast local images finish before the dialog handle is created; repeated filtering cannot repair the stale loading marker.

Recommended fix

Begin thumbnail work after handle creation/shown. Remove loading markers on every outcome on the UI thread, use a lifetime/generation token, and transfer or dispose each image exactly once in a callback that rechecks lifetime.

Regression protection

Force worker completion before handle creation, after close, and across reset. Verify retry is possible and every bitmap has one owner.

M12 · The All filter launches unbounded full-image decoding and retains every thumbnail

MediumLikelyFix effort: Medium

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/StatisticsForm.cs
Method / type: RefreshStatistics / QueueThumbnailLoad / CreateThumbnail
Lines: 1426–1485, 2332–2334, 2397–2439

Failure mechanism

Every existing row launches Task.Run, including off-screen rows. All/Neglected can queue an entire large collection; each task decodes the original image before cropping to 80×45, and the cache has no eviction before form close. There is no concurrency cap or cancellation. Large/slow collections can consume substantial memory, disk bandwidth and thread-pool capacity, and closing the dialog does not stop the queued decoding work.

Circumstances / confidence

Thousands of wallpapers, high-resolution images, network storage, or rapidly opening/closing Statistics. Resource impact is inferred from the queue/decoder path, not a destructive load test.

Recommended fix

Load only visible/near-visible rows, cap decode concurrency, cancel queued work on close, and use a bounded LRU cache. Keep file enumeration/metadata work off the UI thread with immutable snapshots.

Regression protection

Stress a large synthetic collection with a controllable decoder; assert bounded in-flight work/cache size and prompt cancellation on close.

M13 · Fixed dialog dimensions exceed common work areas without a recovery layout

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Medium

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/StatisticsForm.cs
Method / type: constructor / fixed layout
Lines: 569–575, 985–1002; SettingsForm.Initialization.cs:74–87, 1530–1569; MainForm.Appearance.cs:301–350

Failure mechanism

Statistics requests a fixed 920×900 client area and places action buttons at y=835. Settings requests 1120×760 with buttons at y=715. There is no work-area fit, scrolling content or responsive repositioning. On a 1366×768 desktop these layouts cannot fit in the available work area; DPI scaling reduces logical space further. MainForm grows up to 766 logical pixels high for its inactive layout. PerMonitorV2 alone cannot correct these fixed coordinates.

Circumstances / confidence

Small laptop displays and higher scaling factors. Geometry is directly established in source; a full device/DPI matrix was not executed.

Recommended fix

Constrain initial dimensions to the active work area, use anchored/table layouts with a scrollable content region and keep dialog actions visible. Re-layout on DPI/work-area changes. Apply a consistent DIP-to-pixel model to custom-drawn widgets as well.

Regression protection

Verify 1366×768 at 100%, 1920×1080 at 150/200%, mixed-DPI moves and longest translations; all controls and actions must remain reachable.

M14 · Several features have no usable keyboard interaction path

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Medium

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/MainForm/MainForm.Initialization.cs
Method / type: settings/about buttons and custom settings controls
Lines: 110–138; SettingsForm.Navigation.cs:46–61; SettingsForm.Initialization.cs:850–869; SettingsForm.ClockPreview.cs:16–59; StatisticsForm.cs:790

Failure mechanism

Settings and About are TabStop=false with glyph-only labels and no corresponding keyboard command. Navigation buttons are also removed from tab order. Clock style selection uses custom Control cards with Click handlers, while the real combo is hidden; no key handler or accessible selection role exposes the card choices. Statistics removes its list from tab order. These choices prevent normal keyboard-only use and make assistive naming/selection unreliable.

Circumstances / confidence

Keyboard-only or screen-reader users; the registered global hotkeys cover slideshow actions, not settings/about or style selection.

Recommended fix

Provide tab stops, meaningful AccessibleName/Role, access keys and keyboard activation/selection for cards, or use standard radio buttons. Keep the statistics list focusable and expose focus/selection in owner drawing.

Regression protection

Navigate the main window and every settings page with Tab/Shift+Tab, arrows, Space and Enter; verify accessible names and selected state with Windows accessibility tooling.

M15 · Settings can report success while persistence fails or only partially completes

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Medium

File: WallpaperControl/Services/AppSettingsStore.cs
Method / type: save methods / WriteValue
Lines: 72–87, 436–485, 762–784; WidgetSettings.cs:118–169; MainForm.Settings.cs:237–244; StatisticsStorage.cs:269–275

Failure mechanism

Many setting writes swallow exceptions entirely; widget/statistics saves only log and return no result. Callers update runtime state and close the settings dialog as though persistence succeeded. Multi-value saves can fail halfway, leaving inconsistent hotkey/widget settings. SetAutostart shows an error but its caller still assigns autostartEnabled to the requested state, so the UI can claim an enabled startup entry that does not exist.

Circumstances / confidence

Registry access denied, storage full, transient profile issues, or one later value failing during a multi-value save.

Recommended fix

Return persistence results, surface a non-destructive save error and retain unsaved state. Prepare/validate values before writes, group related settings into a versioned snapshot where practical, and read back autostart state after failure.

Regression protection

Inject denied writes and failure halfway through a settings save. Verify no false saved indication, consistent retry behavior and correct autostart state.

M16 · A transient primary-file read failure can turn backup recovery into data rollback

MediumLikelyFix effort: Medium

File: WallpaperControl/Data/StatisticsStorage.cs
Method / type: Load / SaveData
Lines: 66–85, 125–159; WallpaperStatistics.cs:69–72, 230–326

Failure mechanism

Load treats all primary read failures, including sharing violations/access errors, as reasons to load the older backup or start empty. It returns no degraded/read-only marker. Once access recovers, a normal RecordView/save can overwrite the newer valid primary with the older in-memory snapshot. The first save retains that newer primary as .bak, but a second save rotates the stale snapshot over it. This differs from the tested corrupt-JSON recovery path.

Circumstances / confidence

A scanner/backup tool or temporary profile access issue blocks statistics.json during startup, then releases it while the app continues saving.

Recommended fix

Distinguish invalid content from transient I/O errors. Retry or enter an explicit read-only/degraded state on access failure; do not write recovered state over an unread primary until reconciliation succeeds. Preserve the recovery source/version and original bytes.

Regression protection

Lock the primary during Load with a readable older backup, unlock, then perform two saves. Verify newer data is not silently discarded.

M17 · The wallpaper lifecycle has no single owner or explicit state model

MediumMaintainabilityFix effort: Large

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/MainForm.cs
Method / type: MainForm and related partial classes
Lines: MainForm.cs:18–305; Forms/MainForm/*; StatisticsForm.cs:531–1059; WidgetManager.cs:134–418

Failure mechanism

Partial files organize code but still share dozens of mutable fields. Native scheduling, custom scheduling, visible host, pause/fullscreen flags, dialogs and saved state are changed by separate entry points. The confirmed cross-component failures in H1, H2 and M1–M3 are concrete consequences. StatisticsForm combines storage projections, list rendering, thumbnail scheduling and dialogs in 3,157 lines; SettingsForm initialization spans 1,614 lines.

Circumstances / confidence

Every new command or lifecycle edge must preserve implicit invariants across these components.

Recommended fix

After correctness fixes, extract an application coordinator with explicit ownership/transition states, injected time/native adapters and cancellable commands. Separate statistics queries and thumbnail ownership from WinForms rendering. Preserve behavior through integration tests before structural changes.

Regression protection

Protect the command/state transition matrix before refactoring. Verify each accepted command has one commit point and all shutdown paths settle active work.

M18 · Standard test invocation succeeds without executing the regression checks

MediumMaintainabilityFix effort: Small

File: WallpaperControl.sln
Method / type: solution and custom regression harness
Lines: solution:5–7; WallpaperControl.RegressionTests.csproj:3–7; RegressionTests/Program.cs:36–41

Failure mechanism

The solution contains only the application. The regression project is a console program without test SDK discovery. dotnet test -c Release exited 0 during this audit while executing zero checks; the separate dotnet run command was required to execute all 121 assertions. A normal CI or reviewer can obtain a green result while bypassing all regression protection.

Circumstances / confidence

Any build pipeline or contributor using the conventional solution-level test command.

Recommended fix

Add the test project to the solution and provide a required CI/test script that runs the harness and checks its exit code, or migrate to a discoverable test framework. Include isolated installer tests in the documented release gate.

Regression protection

Make a deliberately failing check fail the standard required test entry point, then restore it. Assert a non-zero executed-test count in CI.

M19 · Hardware initialization and shutdown can block the UI thread

MediumLikelyFix effort: Medium

File: WallpaperControl/Services/SystemMonitorService.cs
Method / type: constructor / Sample / Dispose
Lines: 52–75, 398–409; SystemWidgetForm.cs:15, 181, 474–482; WidgetManager.cs:257–268

Failure mechanism

Sampling runs on Task.Run, but the Computer.Open call occurs synchronously while constructing the widget on the UI thread. Dispose is also called on the UI thread and waits for the same lock held through all hardware updates, network and drive queries. A slow driver/hardware call therefore blocks enabling/disabling a widget or closing the app; moving only Sample to a worker does not isolate the full lifetime. An Open exception also escapes construction without cleanup of partially opened resources.

Circumstances / confidence

Hardware with slow/failing sensor access or a sample still running when the widget is disabled. No problematic driver was deliberately invoked.

Recommended fix

Move open/sample/close onto one owned background worker with observable initialization errors and asynchronous shutdown. Keep the UI free of the sampling lock; define a bounded shutdown strategy for native calls that cannot be cancelled.

Regression protection

Use a fake monitor whose Open/Sample blocks and throws. Confirm UI interaction and close initiation remain responsive and partial initialization is cleaned up.

M20 · A rejection target equal to the source only renames the image inside the slideshow

MediumConfirmedFix effort: Small

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/MainForm/MainForm.Rejection.cs
Method / type: GetRejectedFolder / RejectCurrentWallpaperAsync
Lines: 60–94, 176–190, 293–328; SettingsForm.cs:147–181

Failure mechanism

The settings dialog validates that the custom rejection root is absolute but does not prevent the effective destination from equalling the wallpaper folder. With subfolders disabled and the same folder selected, GetUniqueDestinationPath sees the original filename and chooses a numbered name. File.Move then renames the image inside the active source folder; it remains eligible and appears again even though Reject reported success. Choosing the source's parent with subfolder mode can produce the same destination.

Circumstances / confidence

A user chooses the wallpaper folder as the custom rejection root, or chooses its parent with source-name subfolders.

Recommended fix

Normalize and compare the effective source/destination directories before advancing or moving. Reject same-directory configurations with a clear message; account for aliases/reparse points where practical. Keep no-overwrite move behavior.

Regression protection

Exercise direct same-folder and parent-plus-subfolder configurations, normal destination collisions and undo collisions.

Low findings

L1 · Some visible content bypasses the otherwise complete resource system

LowConfirmedFix effort: Small

File: WallpaperControl/Services/IcsCalendarProvider.cs
Method / type: ToCalendarEvent and user-visible formatting
Lines: 304; SystemWidgetForm.cs:297; SettingsForm.ClockPreview.cs:150; MainForm.Initialization.cs:354–362

Failure mechanism

Untitled events become the German literal '(ohne Titel)' regardless of language. Drive text includes 'GB frei', the clock preview always renders '13. September 2026', and transition durations use hard-coded comma decimals. Weather and several file-size strings use the process formatting culture rather than Localization.CurrentCulture; ApplyLanguage changes only UI culture. The five resource files have full key/placeholder parity, so parity checks cannot detect these bypasses.

Circumstances / confidence

Choose English, French, Spanish or Japanese, especially when the OS number culture differs from the app language.

Recommended fix

Move genuine prose/fallbacks into resources and format user-visible values with the selected culture. Use a real sample date formatted with the preview language. Keep stable persisted folder names such as Aussortiert unchanged unless a migration is intentionally designed.

Regression protection

Check untitled events, disk rows, clock preview and duration labels in all five languages with an OS culture different from the selected language.

L2 · An unused COM declaration has the wrong managed return shape

LowPotentialFix effort: Trivial

File: WallpaperControl/Interop/Interop.cs
Method / type: IDesktopWallpaper.Enable
Lines: 180–183

Failure mechanism

Native Enable returns an HRESULT and has one input BOOL, with no output retval. Without PreserveSig, the managed signature should return void. The current bool return incorrectly describes a marshalled retval. Repository searches found no caller, so there is no established current runtime failure; it is a latent interop defect.

Circumstances / confidence

A future caller begins using Enable, or the declaration is reused.

Recommended fix

Change to void Enable([MarshalAs(UnmanagedType.Bool)] bool enable), or explicitly preserve and check an int HRESULT. Verify the full interface against the SDK, not a copied declaration.

void Enable([MarshalAs(UnmanagedType.Bool)] bool enable);

Regression protection

Add a signature-contract check and a controlled COM integration test if the method becomes used.

L3 · Update dialogs do not dispose the Fonts they allocate

LowConfirmedFix effort: Small

File: WallpaperControl/Forms/UpdateDialog.cs
Method / type: constructor / owned fonts
Lines: 83, 100, 112; class has no Dispose override

Failure mechanism

Three Font objects are allocated and assigned to the form/labels without an owner disposal path. Disposing controls does not transfer ownership of caller-created fonts. Other dialogs already track owned fonts, but UpdateDialog does not, leaving native/font resources to nondeterministic finalization after repeated checks.

Circumstances / confidence

Repeated manual update dialogs or long-running automatic update prompts.

Recommended fix

Use the same explicit owned-font list/Dispose pattern as SettingsForm and AboutForm, disposing after controls no longer use the fonts.

Regression protection

Open/close many injected-result update dialogs and inspect resource retention without relying on forced GC.

L4 · Native drawing failures are silent and no upload success is observable

LowPotentialFix effort: Small

File: WallpaperControl/Widgets/LayeredWidgetBitmap.cs
Method / type: Update
Lines: 20–50

Failure mechanism

GetDC, CreateCompatibleDC, SelectObject and UpdateLayeredWindow results are not validated. Cleanup generally releases successfully acquired handles, which the existing GDI regression check supports, but an upload failure leaves the widget stale/invisible with no diagnostic. The test checks handle-count stability, not successful rendering. No upload failure was reproduced.

Circumstances / confidence

GDI resource pressure, an invalid/destroyed handle or a native upload rejection.

Recommended fix

Validate acquisition and upload results, capture GetLastWin32Error where supported, and return a result so the owner can retry/recreate or show a bounded diagnostic. Keep the existing finally-based cleanup.

Regression protection

Inject failing native calls and verify cleanup, a reported failure and bounded retry; retain the handle-leak regression.

CA1031 — broad catches (126)
Some protect intentional UI/native boundaries. Others hide failed application state transitions or persistence; see M8, M15 and M16. Catching broadly is not by itself a defect; callers need an observable outcome.
CA2213 / CA2000 — ownership (117 / 8)
Do not interpret these as 125 established leaks. Most child controls are disposed through their parent; several frames transfer ownership to a host, and HttpClient owns its handler. Cancellation sources with explicit interlocked/using ownership require path-sensitive review. Exception-only allocations still deserve care. Independently established font ownership is L3; timer/task lifetimes are M9–M12.
CA2007 / CA1849 / CA2025 — async (44 / 4 / 3)
WinForms awaits often need UI-context continuation, so blanket ConfigureAwait(false) is unsafe. All three CA2025 test cases synchronously complete the task through GetAwaiter().GetResult before leaving the using scope; they are not proven escaping-disposal defects. Native sampling on the UI path is independently discussed in M19.
CA1303 / CA1305 and other globalization rules
Literal messages and formatting need user-facing review (L1); log/test strings need not all become resources. Resource-key/format-placeholder parity passes for all five languages, but does not validate translation semantics, hard-coded values or layout.
CA5392 / CA5394 / CA5399 — security (14 / 5 / 1)
CA5392 appears only in the regression assembly compiling linked P/Invokes. Production Program applies DefaultDllImportSearchPaths(System32). Random is used for presentation/shuffling, not cryptographic secrets. The update HTTP handler disables certificate revocation checks (CA5399), a hardening opportunity; normal HTTPS certificate validation is not disabled.
CA1806 and remaining style/performance rules
Ignored native results overlap the robustness concern in L4; cosmetic titlebar API failures have lower impact. Formatting caches, collection/interface specialization, static members, initializers and constant arrays are lower priority. CA1823 identifies unused MOD_WIN. CA1508 needs exception-path context before removing a guard. These are not inflated into separate runtime findings.

Architecture and duplication observations

Partial forms split files but retain a single shared mutable state model. The primary problem is ownership: native wallpaper state, the persistent host, scheduler, history commands, settings and widgets each make decisions about the same session without a single transaction boundary (H1–H2, M1–M3, M7–M8, M17). Extract a slideshow session coordinator with explicit renderer readiness, current frame, pause reasons, transition cancellation and a single commit operation before moving UI code mechanically.

StatisticsForm spans 3,157 lines and SettingsForm.Initialization spans 1,614. Thumbnail decode/cache/lifecycle policy should live outside StatisticsForm; settings should edit a model and commit through services with success/failure results. Shared update presentation should return a typed action, eliminating the duplicated OK/Yes contract (M5). A widget lifecycle helper can make handle creation, refresh cancellation, suspension and timer activation consistent (M4, M10).

Persistence already has useful atomic-write machinery, but callers need an explicit outcome and degraded-read state (M15–M16). Keep these concepts centralized rather than proliferating silent catch-and-default wrappers. Avoid broad refactoring before adding failure-path tests around the current behavior.

Test coverage gaps

The harness contains meaningful policy, persistence, IPC and native-resource checks; the 121 count includes individual assertions rather than 121 independently discovered test cases. It does not start the real slideshow UI as a complete desktop session. Passing checks therefore leave important interactions unprotected (M18).

GapConcrete regression to addFinding
Renderer acquisition and topologyAttach failure, Explorer restart, two monitors, Span, negative coordinates and display change.H1, H2
Candidate decodingValid/corrupt/valid sequential folder and bounded automatic errors.H3
Untrusted calendar volumeLimit response bytes, event/occurrence counts, expansion duration, row/bitmap dimensions; enforce cancellation.H4
Transition state ownershipPause/pin/close during an awaited animation; select history image while renderer is active.M1, M2
Scheduler overdue behaviorLarge injected clock jump/resume, one bounded tick and next future deadline.M3
Form startup/disposalCalendar OnShown starts periodic refresh; weather refresh finishes after disposal; update owner closes while awaiting.M4, M9, M10
Action and settings contractsUpdate action reaches shell opener; externally loaded position reaches renderer; failed folder application cannot appear saved.M5, M7, M8
Sensitive controlsActual multiline password masking behavior and Show/Hide presentation.M6
ThumbnailsCompletion before handle creation, closure while callbacks are queued, bounded concurrency/cache.M11, M12
Persistence failuresRead-sharing failure followed by two saves, denied writes, full disk and partial multi-setting commits.M15, M16
User-visible integrationSmall work area at 150–200% DPI, keyboard-only navigation, translated layouts, rejection to same folder.M13, M14, M20
Native ownership and installerHardware sampling shutdown under load, upload-success verification, upgrade/uninstall/autostart matrix.M19, L3, L4

Retain the real pipe child-process tests and statistics replacement/backup tests. Add a CI entry point that explicitly runs the harness, fails on a failed check, and reports the assertion count; dotnet test alone currently provides false assurance.

Security observations

The realistic untrusted-input surface is calendar content fetched from configured URLs. H4 concerns resource exhaustion inside the desktop user process: an apparently bounded date window does not bound the number of recurrences or rendered rows. This does not require privilege escalation. M6 exposes private calendar URLs visually despite protection at rest; DPAPI protection remains a separate useful control.

IPC uses a current-user-only named pipe, a user-specific name, bounded commands and a deadline, and accepts only the supported show/next actions. No arbitrary command or caller-supplied filesystem path is executed through the pipe. The user-scoped single-instance mechanism and pipe behavior have regression protection. Cross-session UX is a policy consideration, not an established cross-user security vulnerability.

The update check begins at a fixed GitHub HTTPS release endpoint and does not download or install executables. A final redirect URI is parsed for a version without a strict destination-host allowlist; an allowlist and certificate-revocation policy are sensible defense in depth, but no attacker-controlled redirect path or TLS bypass was established. Configured HTTP calendars are intentionally fetchable and can reveal content over an unencrypted connection; this is a client fetch, not a server-side SSRF trust boundary.

Production P/Invokes restrict DLL search to System32. DPAPI uses per-user protection and matching native allocation cleanup. Wallpaper file actions validate image paths and use ArgumentList for Explorer arguments; no shell command-string injection was established. Rejection uses non-overwriting moves rather than deletion, although M20 breaks the user’s intended exclusion when the destination resolves to the source location.

The installer is per-user/lowest-privilege, has a stable application identity, and preserves profile data on uninstall. Autostart cleanup matches the installed command to avoid removing another copy’s startup entry. Publish staging and cleanup are constrained to their intended paths. These are source observations; live installer behavior and dependency advisories remain unverified.

Positive engineering observations

  • Statistics persistence uses unique same-directory temporary files, flush-to-disk, replacement/backup and corrupt-file quarantine; tests exercise recovery and locking. This is a solid foundation despite the transient-read ambiguity in M16.
  • Native COM references are generally released in finally blocks, and shell creation checks HRESULTs. Layered bitmap cleanup has a repeated GDI-handle regression check.
  • Fullscreen policy preserves manual pause and tests its grace interval separately from the actual desktop. Injected time and hotkey adapters make policy behavior testable.
  • Widget previews clone state and restore it on cancellation; position changes are committed deliberately. Calendar partial-source outages preserve useful cached results, with regression coverage.
  • Rejection avoids overwrite and supports undo without clobbering collisions. It attempts to change the displayed wallpaper before moving the old image.
  • Most forms track owned fonts explicitly. Logging rotates at a bounded size and is designed not to crash the app on logging failures.
  • All five resource files have 323 matching keys and compatible format placeholders; literal Localization.Get references resolve. This is useful structural protection, although it does not catch L1.

Recommended remediation roadmap

  1. Protect user state and input boundaries. Bound calendar download/expansion/rendering (H4); make writes observable and prevent transient-read fallback from overwriting newer statistics (M15–M16); correct the private-URL presentation (M6) and same-folder rejection behavior (M20). Add the corresponding failure fixtures first.
  2. Restore slideshow reliability. Make renderer acquisition transactional with fallback (H1), define multi-monitor ownership (H2), skip unreadable candidates (H3), unify history/manual changes (M1), and cancel/commit transitions consistently on pause, pin and shutdown (M2). Verify on a disposable multi-monitor Windows session.
  3. Fix bounded scheduling and form lifetime. Address overdue scheduler deadlines (M3), calendar startup (M4), weather/update disposal races (M9–M10), thumbnail lifecycle and load bounds (M11–M12), and hardware sampling ownership (M19). Add deterministic tests using injected clocks and blocked completions.
  4. Repair small contracts and usability. Correct update dialog results (M5), settings-position propagation (M7), folder-change outcomes (M8), small-display layout (M13), keyboard access (M14), and localization/font ownership (L1, L3).
  5. Make the checks unavoidable, then simplify. Integrate the custom harness in CI (M18); extract coordinator and thumbnail/lifecycle services behind those tests (M17). Follow with native error observability and unused interop correction (L2, L4), then justified analyzer/style improvements. Do not blanket-suppress or mechanically “fix” ownership/async warnings.

Overall assessment

The repository demonstrates care in recovery, IPC restrictions, file collision safety and low-level cleanup. Its largest weakness is orchestration: independently plausible methods do not consistently agree on who owns the current wallpaper, when a control is usable, or whether a requested change actually succeeded. The passing regression suite is valuable, but concentrates on components rather than those boundaries.

Prioritize the High findings and state/lifecycle defects before treating the clean Release build as a production-readiness signal. Multi-monitor and shell recovery need live validation after fixes; calendar resource limits and persistence failure behavior need adversarial fixtures. The recommended changes can build on existing seams, without discarding the application’s useful test and persistence infrastructure.
